sanskrit: tad drumāṇāṃ śilānāṃ ca varṣaṃ prāṇaharaṃ mahat pratijagrāha dharmātmā rāghavas tīkṣṇasāyakaiḥ
english: That deadly shower of trees and boulders, the righteous Rāghava received and intercepted with his sharp arrows.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tad varaṃ nimīlita ivarṣabhaḥ rāmaḥ krodhaṃ paraṃ bheje vadhārthaṃ sarvarakṣasām
english: Having received that onslaught, like a bull with eyes half-closed, Rāma gathered his supreme wrath for the purpose of slaying all the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: tataḥ krodhasamāviṣṭaḥ pradīpta iva tejasā śarair abhyakirat sainyaṃ sarvataḥ sahadūṣaṇam
english: Then, seized by fury and blazing as though with inner fire, he rained arrows upon the entire host together with Dūṣaṇa from all sides.

sanskrit: tataḥ senāpatiḥ kruddho dūṣaṇaḥ śatrudūṣaṇaḥ jagrāha giriśṛṅgābhaṃ parighaṃ romaharṣaṇam
english: Then the enraged general Dūṣaṇa, destroyer of enemies, seized a bar-mace resembling a mountain peak, terrible enough to make one's hair stand on end.

sanskrit: veṣṭitaṃ kāñcanaiḥ paṭṭair devasainyābhimardanam āyasaiḥ śaṅkubhis tīkṣṇaiḥ kīrṇaṃ paravasokṣitām
english: It was wrapped in bands of gold, a crusher of divine armies, bristling with sharp iron spikes, and drenched with the fat of enemies.

sanskrit: vajrāśanisamasparśaṃ paragopuradāraṇam taṃ mahoragasaṃkāśaṃ pragṛhya parighaṃ raṇe dūṣaṇo 'bhyapatad rāmaṃ krūrakarmā niśācaraḥ
english: Terrifying to the touch like the vajra and the thunderbolt, a splitter of enemy citadels, resembling a great serpent — seizing that bar-mace, the cruel-actioned night-roamer Dūṣaṇa flew at Rāma in battle.

sanskrit: tasyābhipatamānasya dūṣaṇasya sa rāghavaḥ dvābhyāṃ śarābhyāṃ ciccheda sahastābharaṇau bhujau
english: As Dūṣaṇa came rushing upon him, Rāghava severed both his arms — ornaments and all — with two arrows.

sanskrit: bhraṣṭas tasya mahākāyaḥ papāta raṇamūrdhani parighaś chinnahastasya śakradhvaja ivāgrataḥ
english: The mace fell from the hands of the severed-armed one and crashed to the forefront of the battlefield, enormous, like Indra's banner toppled.

sanskrit: sa karābhyāṃ vikīrṇābhyāṃ papāta bhuvi dūṣaṇaḥ viṣāṇābhyāṃ viśīrṇābhyāṃ manasvīva mahāgajaḥ
english: His arms scattered wide, Dūṣaṇa fell to the earth like a great spirited elephant whose tusks have been broken off.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā taṃ patitaṃ bhūmau dūṣaṇaṃ nihataṃ raṇe sādhu sādhv iti kākutsthaṃ sarvabhūtāny apūjayan
english: Seeing Dūṣaṇa fallen slain on the battlefield, all living beings cried out "Well done! Well done!" and honoured Kākutstha.

sanskrit: etasminn antare kruddhās trayaḥ senāgrayāyinaḥ saṃhatyābhyadravan rāmaṃ mṛtyupāśāvapāśitāḥ mahākapālaḥ sthūlākṣaḥ pramāthī ca mahābalaḥ
english: At that moment three enraged vanguard commanders, ensnared by the noose of death, joined forces and charged at Rāma: Mahākapāla, Sthūlākṣa, and the mighty Pramāthin.

sanskrit: mahākapālo vipulaṃ śūlam udyamya rākṣasaḥ sthūlākṣaḥ paṭṭiśaṃ gṛhya pramāthī ca paraśvadham
english: The rākṣasa Mahākapāla raised a huge spear, Sthūlākṣa seized a broad sword, and Pramāthin took up a battle-axe.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaivāpatatas tāṃs tu rāghavaḥ sāyakaiḥ śitaiḥ tīkṣṇāgraiḥ pratijagrāha saṃprāptān atithīn iva
english: Seeing those three rushing at him, Rāghava received them with sharp, keen-tipped arrows as one receives guests who have arrived.

sanskrit: mahākapālasya śiraś ciccheda raghunaṅganaḥ asaṃkhyeyais tu bāṇaughaiḥ pramamātha pramāthinam
english: The scion of Raghu severed Mahākapāla's head and crushed Pramāthin with countless floods of arrows.

sanskrit: sthūlākṣasyākṣiṇī tīkṣṇaiḥ pūrayām āsa sāyakaiḥ sa papāta hato bhūmau viṭapīva mahādrumaḥ
english: He filled Sthūlākṣa's eyes with sharp arrows; Sthūlākṣa fell slain to the ground like a great branching tree cut down.

sanskrit: tataḥ pāvakasaṃkāśair hemavajravibhūṣitaiḥ jaghanaśeṣaṃ tejasvī tasya sainyasya sāyakaiḥ
english: Then, with arrows blazing like fire and adorned with gold and iron, the radiant Rāma slew the remainder of that army.

sanskrit: te rukmapuṅkhā viśikhāḥ sadhūmā iva pāvakāḥ nijaghnus tāni rakṣāṃsi vajrā iva mahādrumān
english: Those gold-fletched, smoke-trailing shafts blazing like fires struck down those rākṣasas as thunderbolts strike down great trees.

sanskrit: rakṣasāṃ tu śataṃ rāmaḥ śatenaikena karṇinā sahasraṃ ca sahasreṇa jaghāna raṇamūrdhani
english: In the vanguard of battle, Rāma slew a hundred rākṣasas with a single hundred of his arrow-swift shafts, and a thousand with a thousand.

sanskrit: tair bhinnavarmābharaṇāś chinnabhinnaśarāsanāḥ nipetuḥ śoṇitādigdhā dharaṇyāṃ rajanīcarāḥ
english: Their armour and ornaments shattered, their bows cut and broken, smeared with blood, those night-roaming rākṣasas fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tair muktakeśaiḥ samare patitaiḥ śoṇitokṣitaiḥ āstīrṇā vasudhā kṛtsnā mahāvediḥ kuśair iva
english: The entire earth, spread with those fallen in battle, their hair loose, drenched in blood, looked like a great sacrificial altar strewn with kuśa grass.

sanskrit: kṣaṇena tu mahāghoraṃ vanaṃ nihatarākṣasaṃ babhūva niraya prakhyaṃ māṃsaśoṇitakardamam
english: In an instant that great dreadful forest, its rākṣasas slain, became a hell-like swamp of flesh and blood.

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām hatāny ekena rāmeṇa mānuṣeṇa padātinā
english: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas of terrible deeds were slain by the single human Rāma, fighting on foot.

sanskrit: tasya sainyasya sarvasya kharaḥ śeṣo mahārathaḥ rākṣasas triśirāś caiva rāmaś ca ripusūdanaḥ
english: Of that entire host, only the great warrior Khara remained, and the rākṣasa Triśiras — and Rāma, the destroyer of foes.

sanskrit: tatas tu tad bhīmabalaṃ mahāhave samīkṣya rāmeṇa hataṃ balīyasā rathena rāmaṃ mahatā kharas tataḥ samāsasādendra ivodyatāśaniḥ
english: Then, seeing that fearsome force destroyed in the great battle by the mighty Rāma, Khara mounted his great chariot and advanced on Rāma, like Indra with his thunderbolt upraised.

sanskrit: kharaṃ tu rāmābhimukhaṃ prayāntaṃ vāhinīpatiḥ rākṣasas triśirā nāma saṃnipatyedam abravīt
english: As Khara advanced toward Rāma, the rākṣasa army-commander named Triśiras intercepted him and spoke these words.

sanskrit: māṃ niyojaya vikrānta saṃnivartasva sāhasāt paśya rāmaṃ mahābāhuṃ saṃyuge vinipātitam
english: "Appoint me instead, O valiant one; withdraw yourself from this rash act. Watch the mighty-armed Rāma laid low in battle."

sanskrit: pratijānāmi te satyam āyudhaṃ cāham ālabhe yathā rāmaṃ vadhiṣyāmi vadhārhaṃ sarvarakṣasām
english: "I swear truly to you and I touch my weapons: I will kill Rāma, who deserves death at the hands of all rākṣasas."

sanskrit: ahaṃ vāsya raṇe mṛtyur eṣa vā samare mama vinivartya raṇotsāhaṃ muhūrtaṃ prāśniko bhava
english: "Either I am death to him in battle, or he is death to me in battle. Restrain your own eagerness to fight; be a spectator for a moment."

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭo vā hate rāme janasthānaṃ prayāsyasi mayi vā nihate rāmaṃ saṃyugāyopayāsyasi
english: "If Rāma is slain, you may return to Janasthāna rejoicing; or if I am slain, you may then come forward to fight Rāma."

sanskrit: kharas triśirasā tena mṛtyulobhāt prasāditaḥ gaccha yudhyety anujñāto rāghavābhimukho yayau
english: Khara, gratified by Triśiras' eagerness for death, gave him permission: "Go, fight!" and Triśiras proceeded toward Rāghava.

sanskrit: triśirāś ca rathenaiva vājiyuktena bhāsvatā abhyadravad raṇe rāmaṃ triśṛṅga iva parvataḥ
english: And Triśiras, mounted on his splendid chariot drawn by swift horses, charged at Rāma in battle like a three-peaked mountain in motion.

sanskrit: śaradhārā samūhān sa mahāmegha ivotsṛjan vyasṛjat sadṛśaṃ nādaṃ jalārdrasyeva dundubheḥ
english: Like a great thundercloud releasing masses of rain-streams, he loosed torrents of arrows and gave forth a sound like a water-drenched war-drum.

sanskrit: āgacchantaṃ triśirasaṃ rākṣasaṃ prekṣya rāghavaḥ dhanuṣā pratijagrāha vidhunvan sāyakāñ śitān
english: Seeing the rākṣasa Triśiras coming at him, Rāghava received him with his bow, shaking out sharp arrows.

sanskrit: sa saṃprahāras tumulo rāma triśirasor mahān babhūvātīva balinoḥ siṃhakuñjarayor iva
english: That tumultuous and great clash between Rāma and Triśiras, both exceedingly powerful, was like the clash between a lion and an elephant.

sanskrit: tatas triśirasā bāṇair lalāṭe tāḍitas tribhiḥ amarṣī kupito rāmaḥ saṃrabdham idam abravīt
english: Then, struck on the forehead by three of Triśiras' arrows, Rāma — impatient, angered, greatly provoked — spoke these words.

sanskrit: aho vikramaśūrasya rākṣasasyedṛśaṃ balam puṣpair iva śarair yasya lalāṭe 'smi parikṣataḥ mamāpi pratigṛhṇīṣva śarāṃś cāpaguṇacyutān
english: "Ah, such is the strength of this brave rākṣasa warrior — I am grazed on the forehead by arrows that feel like flowers! Now receive my arrows too, discharged from the bowstring."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu saṃrabdhaḥ śarān āśīviṣopamān triśiro vakṣasi kruddho nijaghāna caturdaśa
english: So saying, in great fury, enraged, he shot fourteen arrows resembling venomous serpents into Triśiras' chest.

sanskrit: caturbhis turagān asya śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ nyapātayata tejasvī caturas tasya vājinaḥ
english: With four well-jointed arrows, the radiant Rāma brought down Triśiras' four horses.

sanskrit: aṣṭabhiḥ sāyakaiḥ sūtaṃ rathopasthe nyapātayat rāmaś ciccheda bāṇena dhvajaṃ cāsya samucchritam
english: With eight arrows he struck down the charioteer onto the floor of the chariot, and with an arrow Rāma also severed Triśiras' upraised banner.

sanskrit: tato hatarathāt tasmād utpatantaṃ niśācaram bibheda rāmas taṃ bāṇair hṛdaye so 'bhavaj jaḍaḥ
english: Then, as the night-roaming rākṣasa leaped from his destroyed chariot, Rāma pierced him in the heart with arrows; he became senseless.

sanskrit: sāyakaiś cāprameyātmā sāmarṣas tasya rakṣasaḥ śirāṃsy apātayat trīṇi vegavadbhis tribhiḥ śataiḥ
english: And the immeasurably great-souled Rāma, with wrath, struck off that rākṣasa's three heads with three swift, powerful arrows.

sanskrit: sa bhūmau śoṇitodgārī rāmabāṇābhipīḍitaḥ nyapatat patitaiḥ pūrvaṃ svaśirobhir niśācaraḥ
english: That night-roamer, pressed by Rāma's arrows and vomiting blood, fell to the ground, his own three heads having fallen before him.

sanskrit: hataśeṣās tato bhagnā rākṣasāḥ kharasaṃśrayāḥ dravanti sma na tiṣṭhanti vyāghratrastā mṛgā iva
english: Then the surviving remnant of the rākṣasas who had taken shelter with Khara broke and fled; they did not stand firm, like deer terrified by a tiger.

sanskrit: tān kharo dravato dṛṣṭvā nivartya ruṣitaḥ svayam rāmam evābhidudrāva rāhuś candramasaṃ yathā
english: Seeing them flee, Khara turned them back in fury, then himself rushed directly at Rāma, as Rāhu rushes at the moon.

sanskrit: nihataṃ dūṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā raṇe triśirasā saha kharasyāpy abhavat trāso dṛṣṭvā rāmasya vikramam
english: Seeing Dūṣaṇa slain in battle together with Triśiras, and witnessing Rāma's prowess, even Khara felt fear.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā rākṣasaṃ sainyam aviṣahyaṃ mahābalam hatam ekena rāmeṇa dūṣaṇas triśirā api
english: Seeing the irresistible, mighty rākṣasa army — and even Dūṣaṇa and Triśiras — slain by the single Rāma,

sanskrit: tad balaṃ hatabhūyiṣṭhaṃ vimanāḥ prekṣya rākṣasaḥ āsasāda kharo rāmaṃ namucir vāsavaṃ yathā
english: that army mostly destroyed — disheartened as he surveyed it, the rākṣasa Khara advanced upon Rāma, as Namuci once advanced upon Vāsava.

sanskrit: vikṛṣya balavac cāpaṃ nārācān raktabhojanān kharaś cikṣepa rāmāya kruddhān āśīviṣān iva
english: Drawing his powerful bow mightily, Khara hurled iron-headed arrows that feed on blood at Rāma, like enraged venomous serpents.

sanskrit: jyāṃ vidhunvan subahuśaḥ śikṣayāstrāṇi darśayan cacāra samare mārgāñ śarai rathagataḥ kharaḥ
english: Snapping his bowstring repeatedly, displaying his mastery of missile-science, Khara on his chariot traced tactical paths across the battlefield with his arrows.

sanskrit: sa sarvāś ca diśo bāṇaiḥ pradiśaś ca mahārathaḥ pūrayām āsa taṃ dṛṣṭvā rāmo 'pi sumahad dhanuḥ
english: The great warrior filled all the cardinal and intermediate directions with arrows; seeing him, Rāma also took up his great bow.

sanskrit: sa sāyakair durviṣahair sasphuliṅgair ivāgnibhiḥ nabhaś cakārāvivaraṃ parjanya iva vṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: With arrows irresistible as spark-shooting fires, he made the sky without gaps, like a rain-cloud with its downpour.

sanskrit: tad babhūva śitair bāṇaiḥ khararāmavisarjitaiḥ paryākāśam anākāśaṃ sarvataḥ śarasaṃkulam
english: The surrounding sky became void of voids — everywhere dense with arrows — from the sharp shafts loosed by Khara and Rāma together.

sanskrit: śarajālāvṛtaḥ sūryo na tadā sma prakāśate anyonyavadhasaṃrambhād ubhayoḥ saṃprayudhyatoḥ
english: The sun did not shine then, enveloped in a net of arrows, as both warriors fought in their mutual fury to kill the other.

sanskrit: tato nālīkanārācais tīkṣṇāgraiś ca vikarṇibhiḥ ājaghāna raṇe rāmaṃ totrair iva mahādvipam
english: Then with nālikā-arrows, iron shafts, and keen-tipped flanged arrows, he struck Rāma in battle as if goading a great elephant with prods.

sanskrit: taṃ rathasthaṃ dhanuṣpāṇiṃ rākṣasaṃ paryavasthitam dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni pāśahastam ivāntakam
english: All living beings beheld that rākṣasa standing in his chariot, bow in hand, looming over the field, like Death himself with his noose in hand.

sanskrit: taṃ siṃham iva vikrāntaṃ siṃhavikrāntagāminam dṛṣṭvā nodvijate rāmaḥ siṃhaḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: Yet seeing him — mighty as a lion, moving with a lion's gait — Rāma felt no alarm, as a lion does not tremble before a lesser beast.

sanskrit: tataḥ sūryanikāśena rathena mahatā kharaḥ āsasāda raṇe rāmaṃ pataṅga iva pāvakam
english: Then on his great chariot blazing like the sun, Khara drew up to Rāma in battle, as a moth draws near to fire.

sanskrit: tato 'sya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ muṣṭideśe mahātmanaḥ kharaś ciccheda rāmasya darśayan pāṇilāghavam
english: Then Khara cut Rāma's bow along with its arrow at the grip, displaying his swiftness of hand against the great-souled Rāma.

sanskrit: sa punas tv aparān sapta śarān ādāya varmaṇi nijaghāna raṇe kruddhaḥ śakrāśanisamaprabhān
english: And then taking up seven more arrows blazing like Indra's thunderbolt, he struck Rāma on his armour in battle, in his fury.

sanskrit: tatas tat prahataṃ bāṇaiḥ kharamuktaiḥ suparvabhiḥ papāta kavacaṃ bhūmau rāmasyādityavarcasaḥ
english: Then that armour of Rāma, radiant as the sun, struck by Khara's well-jointed arrows, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: sa śarair arpitaḥ kruddhaḥ sarvagātreṣu rāghavaḥ rarāja samare rāmo vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan
english: Thus pierced by arrows in all his limbs and incensed with anger, Rāghava blazed in battle like a smokeless fire burning.

sanskrit: tato gambhīranirhrādaṃ rāmaḥ śatrunibarhaṇaḥ cakārāntāya sa ripoḥ sajyam anyan mahad dhanuḥ
english: Then Rāma, crusher of enemies, strung another great bow with a deep resounding twang, for the annihilation of his foe.

sanskrit: sumahad vaiṣṇavaṃ yat tad atisṛṣṭaṃ maharṣiṇā varaṃ tad dhanur udyamya kharaṃ samabhidhāvata
english: Taking up that supremely great Vaiṣṇava bow which had been bestowed as a gift by the great sage, he rushed against Khara.

sanskrit: tataḥ kanakapuṅkhais tu śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ ciccheda rāmaḥ saṃkruddhaḥ kharasya samare dhvajam
english: Then with gold-fletched, well-jointed arrows, the greatly enraged Rāma cut down Khara's battle standard in the fight.

sanskrit: sa darśanīyo bahudhā vicchinnaḥ kāñcano dhvajaḥ jagāma dharaṇīṃ sūryo devatānām ivājñayā
english: That beautiful golden banner, severed in many pieces, fell to the earth like the sun descending at the gods' command.

sanskrit: taṃ caturbhiḥ kharaḥ kruddho rāmaṃ gātreṣu mārgaṇaiḥ vivyādha hṛdi marmajño mātaṅgam iva tomaraiḥ
english: Enraged, Khara, knowing the vital points, pierced Rāma in the limbs with four arrows and in the heart — as one might goad a great elephant with lances.

sanskrit: sa rāmo bahubhir bāṇaiḥ kharakārmukaniḥsṛtaiḥ viddho rudhirasiktāṅgo babhūva ruṣito bhṛśam
english: Rāma, pierced by many arrows discharged from Khara's bow, his limbs drenched with blood, became exceedingly incensed.

sanskrit: sa dhanur dhanvināṃ śreṣṭhaḥ pragṛhya paramāhave mumoca parameṣvāsaḥ ṣaṭ śarān abhilakṣitān
english: He, the foremost of archers and supreme bowman, gripping his bow in the great battle, released six well-aimed arrows.

sanskrit: śirasy ekena bāṇena dvābhyāṃ bāhvor athārpayat tribhiś candrārdhavaktraiś ca vakṣasy abhijaghāna ha
english: With one arrow he struck Khara on the head; with two he struck him on both arms; and with three crescent-faced arrows he smote him on the chest.

sanskrit: tataḥ paścān mahātejā nārācān bhāskaropamān jighāṃsū rākṣasaṃ kruddhas trayodaśa śilāśitān
english: Then afterwards, the great-splendoured Rāma, desirous of killing the rākṣasa and enraged, took up thirteen iron arrows whetted on stone, blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: tato 'sya yugam ekena caturbhiś caturo hayān ṣaṣṭhena ca śiraḥ saṃkhye ciccheda kharasāratheḥ
english: Then with one arrow he cut the yoke, with four he felled the four horses, and with the sixth in battle he severed the head of Khara's charioteer.

sanskrit: tribhis triveṇuṃ balavān dvābhyām akṣaṃ mahābalaḥ dvādaśena tu bāṇena kharasya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ chittvā vajranikāśena rāghavaḥ prahasann iva trayodaśenendrasamo bibheda samare kharam
english: With three he destroyed the triple-bamboo chariot-pole, the mighty one with two cut the axle, with the twelfth arrow he severed Khara's bow together with its arrow; and then, smiling as it were, with the thirteenth — blazing like the vajra — Rāghava, equal to Indra, pierced Khara in battle.

sanskrit: prabhagnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ gadāpāṇir avaplutya tasthau bhūmau kharas tadā
english: His bow shattered, his chariot destroyed, his horses slain, his charioteer killed, Khara then leaped down and stood on the ground, mace in hand.

sanskrit: tat karma rāmasya mahārathasya sametya devāś ca maharṣayaś ca apūjayan prāñjalayaḥ prahṛṣṭās tadā vimānāgragatāḥ sametāḥ
english: At that feat of the great warrior Rāma, the gods and the great sages gathered there, stationed at the prows of their celestial vehicles, rejoiced and honoured him with joined palms.
